What more could be said about Skyrim that has not already been?
At least, personally, I thought it had an "okay" story.  Really, it feels more like a sandbox to screw around in but with a few rules on a sign next to it. Barely anyone enforces it, and you're likely going to bring your own toys into it. Hell, some people remodel the whole thing, and only trained observers and pick out that it was built on/around/quantumly the sandbox that was there.
...Summarily put, it's something modded. You're going to mod this, even if its just bugfixes for stability, you're going to play this modded.

I think the one takeaway I had, however, was generally what Parthurnaax had to say. Personally the most intriguing character, and handsome to boot. Namely, to paraphrase, "Is it better to be born good, or to overcome your evil through effort"?

My advice is that if you don't own it, if you haven't played it, don't start. Play other games. Your time is wasted here. It's a nothingburger that tastes good.

There's not much to it. I did the story, I've played the faction quests, I've been the servant to everyone from peasants to daedric princes. And no doubt, I'm going to keep doing it. But there's something vapid about it all. Something is missing that I can't quite but into words. The mechanics, the story, the gameplay loop, it all lacks depth. But maybe I just know exactly how deep it goes, so I'm not impressed anymore.

Maybe this is all just because I'm on my tenth playthrough. I've seen it all before, so the feeling of magic is lost. Maybe the long time favorites of mine that I'm comparing it to, like terraria, gmod, and hitman, just have more replayability, and that shouldn't disqualify skyrim like I'm suggesting. But I can't help but feel the way I do. Whatever. I'm leaving this review negative because fuck bethesda

The Skyrim SE is an 64 bit game and uses all the RAM you can spare. While the game is awesome, it is also awesomely bugged...! It does not release previously used RAM - but swaps it out to a Swap file. If swap too small, it will crash... I've increased my swap file to min 128GB / max 256GB and SkyrimSE uses 130GB of it easily. Once this happens, the loading screens can take a minute or two. I must close the game then and reopen to clear the RAM usage. I've played it in 2016 and came back now to see the x64 'remastered' version. Skyrim SE is beautiful, reminds me of my beautiful girlified who i loved and hated for her constant mood crashes.
Disclaimer - i did not purchase the extra Creations DLC, it's as i purchased it 10 years ago - with whatever came free as of 2026.

This game is amazing. Even though it came out 15 years ago, this game still holds up today as one of the best open world games I have ever played. The story isn't anything to write home about, but that's not what makes this game is special. It's a magical feeling when you take a random road or find a random dungeon. And when you get to the end of these dungeons or roads you find special pieces of gear that are very cool, fun, and rewarding. This game rewards you for slowing down and looking and places that are off the beaten path. Mix that with the amazing ability to actually feel like you are roleplaying as an ancient Nord warrior, and the ability to make your own decisions at times makes this game one of the best if you are looking for the open world adventure genre.

10/10 dialogue for a GUARD! For the THIRD GAME IN A ROW! Elder Scrolls continues to be the only game series that can pull me into the world with the fifth entry, Skyrim, teaching me to embrace my Dovahkiin roots. This is hands down my favorite game in the franchise with it containing a certain magically charm often referred to as "Lightning in a Bottle" and it really cannot be understated how true this is. Sure, the world is a little TOO big and there are lots of fields and trees with random events happening either far too often or never enough with a litany of common knowledge bugs and tricks players have come to know over the years that can isolate new-comers to the game but to me, it is more than that. Skyrim is so amazing because it exists beyond its issues and is seen as a whole. Sure devs can make the game super easy and straight forward and linear but our real world is far from those things so why make Tamriel like this? A game with constant dopamine rushes will burn out your brain and cause a crash. When i finally find a sweet roll in Skyrim, whether the first or 10,000th, I'm getting excited and taking it. Caves can feel empty, things repetitive, and towns small because well, towns ARE small! Caves ARE empty! (usually ;) ) and yes, life can get repetitive, that's not Skyrim's fault! 

So why play it? You get so absorbed you as a player begin to exist now not as yourself, but as THE Dragonborn. Maybe for you personally, games can pull you in and you love to roleplay, as do I, but in the end, it is always just a game, no matter how fun or immersed my roleplay is, potentially unlike you. HOWEVER!!! When I play Skyrim... Oh Baby.... its the only time in my life I'm not just moving a controller stick or pressing keys or typing because, as cringe as it may be, I am living my magical and medieval second life. I Loved Skyrim: Anniversary Edition on Steam and mods were all I could have expected and more! <3 Nothing can ever make me feel as if I am doing anything more than playing a game until I load into Skyrim and and ask myself, "what do I WANT to do Today?" because in Skyrim, ESPECIALLY with mods, it is the only time i believe i can do anything I want.
